rows: A tornado uprooted a large mesquite tree and willow tree. The mesquite tree was approximately 4 feet wide at the base.
The large hail stones damaged vehicle windshields in Moran.
A trained spotter reported and photgraphed a well developed cone tornado in rural northwest Shakelford County. The tornado remaind on the ground for several minutes over open range land.
A 65 mph gust produced only minor damage to structures.
Telephone poles were blown down around Albany.
The severe thunderstorm winds in Albany blew shingles off of roofs, and the intense winds also toppled telephone poles.
Baseball size hail was reported near the intersection of Highways 351 and 604.
A storm chaser reported a brief tornado about 4 miles northeast of Albany.
Law enforcement reported a broken windshield from the hail.
This report was relayed to the National Weather Service by the Abilene Police Department.
A National Weather Service Cooperative Observer reported large limbs were blown down by strong thunderstorm winds.
A power line was reported down in Albany. The time was estimated by radar.
A trained spotter reported broken six inch diameter tree limbs near Moran along State Highway 6.
Law enforcement reported a roof was torn off of a house and power lines were blown down on the north side of Albany.
The sheriff's office estimated a 60 mph wind gust.
The fire department reported a large factory lost its roof. In addition, several very large trees and power lines were downed by the strong winds.

A trained spotter reported a wind gust of 60 mph, 4 miles north of Moran.
A member of the public took a photo of this tornado that was illuminated by lightning. This tornado was quite tall.
Law enforcement officials reported damaging thunderstorm winds blew tree limbs down and caused some roof damage in Albany. The thunderstorm winds also damaged a door at the courthouse.

This tornado began just inside Jones County northeast of Abilene and crossed into southwest Shackelford County. There was a report of debris deposited along the Jones and Shackelford County lines. Radar also showed a debris ball signature in this area.
A trained spotter reported quarter size hail covering the roadway.
The time of this hail report was estimated by radar.

The public reported broken tree limbs on a residents property. The winds were estimated at 60 mph. The time was estimated using velocity data.
Law Enforcement reported baseball size hail at Fort Griffin.
